data.name: Ajaam
data.gender_notes: Ajaam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root letters 'A-J-M'. In Islamic history, Ajaam is a name given to a person who collects and gathers people, particularly in religious or scholarly contexts. This name is also mentioned in the Quran, where it refers to a group of people who opposed Prophet Ibrahim (AS). The name Ajaam carries the meaning “Gatherer of people” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ajaam usually hope their child will grow to embody gatherer of people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes unity and community.
data.etymology: Ajaam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gatherer of people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ajaam total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
